(A) The guard regressed, so the single-design open mints silently again.
(B) A second open path (the registry) never got the guard's loudness.

④ WHAT SEPARATES THEM. A predicts a stdio or --http open of a store whose sidecars are gone to succeed with a new id. B predicts --registry-root to list nothing and say nothing about the directory. D predicts the Dockerfile to still say "silently" while the code refuses.

⑤ RESULTS (scratch store with two requirements written, then its graph directory copied alone, without the sidecars):
· stdio --graph-path: REFUSED. Degraded surface, and the handshake plus stderr say "the design at … has lost its identity file … reflow2 will not guess … If this is a container, the usual cause is a volume mounted at the store directory instead of its parent — mount the parent."
· --http --graph-path: REFUSED the same way, and the server stays up serving `reflow2_unavailable` with the reason. ⇒ A REFUTED.
· --registry-root over a root whose one design directory holds that store: stderr says "WARNING — no designs found under reg. … A design is a directory containing a reflow2 store." GET / says "This server's registry root holds no designs." POST /g/<its old id>/mcp says "no design named `…` is registered here". Nothing names the directory, the data in it, or the missing identity file. registry.rs Registry::discover keeps only DesignPathState::Design, and discover.rs already classifies this directory as Unnamed ("A store directory is there with no identity beside it"), which is dropped. ⇒ B HOLDS: this path reads as empty, in the reporter's words.
· Dockerfile:77-81 (last changed 2026-09-13) still says a store opened without its sidecar "finds nothing and PRESENTS AS AN EMPTY DESIGN, reporting nothing wrong", which has been false for the single-design path since 2026-08-07. The issue says "Your Dockerfile notes do warn about this". ⇒ D PARTLY HOLDS: the warning is stale for one path and accidentally true for the other.
· C: not separately measured; the guard reads only graph.id.json.
· Aside: the refused open still wrote a fresh graph.meta.json beside the store it refused.

⑥ CLASS: one condition, a store with data and no identity, is judged on two paths, and only the one written first reports it. The loud refusal (2026-08-07) was put on the open path. The registry (2026-08-12) correctly never opens an Unnamed store, but discards the classification it already has. The same class as the degraded-surface finding from this same issue: a verdict reached on one path and not carried to its sibling. A fix at the class would carry Unnamed through: startup names each Unnamed directory with the missing file, and the empty-listing and unknown-id replies count and name them. It would also correct the Dockerfile text, so the warning says what the code does.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE (no code changed). A test pinning the class: a registry root holding a store with content and no graph.id.json. Its startup output and its unknown-id and empty-listing replies all name that directory and the missing identity file, and never say "no designs" while an Unnamed store is present. Plus a doc check that the Dockerfile's sidecar paragraph matches the refusal the code gives.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "silently comes up looking empty" is QUALIFIED. It is true of --registry-root and false of a single-design server, which refuses loudly. "Mount the parent" HOLDS as the right advice, and the code's own refusal gives it.
